newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Egyptian in drugs case released from Cyprus jail.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian in drugs case released from Cyprus jail.

text.p: Prison authorities in Cyprus discharged an Egyptian jailed for drugs possession after a court of appeal ruled his arrest was a police set-up, officials said on Thursday.
"We released him immediately after the court decision yesterday," a source at the central prisons in capital Nicosia told Reuters.
Restaurant owner Mousa Hady Haggag, 40, was jailed for 12 years in October 1995 on charges of possessing 30 kg (66 lb) of hashish with the purpose of selling it.

Haggag, a permanent resident of Cyprus, was arrested in July 1995 immediately after receiving the narcotics at a designated pick-up point in an operation organised by an undercover police officer. The decision said undercover officers encouraged Haggag to take part in the operation.
The person who dropped the narcotics off was never caught.
"It is neither accepted nor tolerated under any circumstance for police to encourage a crime so as to solve it," said the decision, issued by Supreme Court President George Pikis.
